description: LLM-oriented codebook for tagging flamenco periodical excerpts. The schema focuses on observable discourse codes, evidence spans, confidence, uncertainty, and derived analytic effects.

annotation_unit.rule: Annotate only the visible review text. A missing code means no visible evidence in the review text, not absence from the full article.
annotation_unit.long_article_rule: If the excerpt is truncated, OCR-damaged, or too short to decide, set insufficient_context=true rather than guessing.

llm_decision_process.name: evidence extraction
llm_decision_process.instruction: Extract candidate spans that contain evaluative, authorizing, excluding, preserving, pedagogical, communal, or critical discourse. Ignore bare keyword hits without discourse function.

llm_decision_process.name: primary code assignment
llm_decision_process.instruction: Assign one or more primary codes only when the extracted span satisfies the required discourse function.

llm_decision_process.name: derived analytic effect
llm_decision_process.instruction: Derive analytic effect, polarity, target, and basis from the primary codes and evidence span.

AUTH.purpose: Track claims that define proper flamenco through genuineness, purity, tradition, roots, continuity, anti-commercial seriousness, or intimate/social authenticity.
AUTH.use_when: Use when passages do evaluative work around what is real, proper, pure, rooted, traditional, continuous, or corrupted flamenco.
AUTH.do_not_use_when: Do not use for neutral chronology, generic praise, advertising, biography, or bare words such as authentic/traditional/pure without flamenco-related evaluative force.

AUTH_01.definition: A discourse move that presents a person, style, repertoire, performance, publication, pedagogy, or practice as genuinely, properly, or truly flamenco.
AUTH_01.use_when: Use when authenticity, truth, genuineness, or properness is asserted, defended, denied, or attributed to a flamenco-related object.
AUTH_01.do_not_use_when: Do not use when authentic/true/proper describes something outside flamenco or generic sincerity/performance success.
required_conditions: The claim concerns flamenco or a flamenco actor/practice.
The passage does more than mention a keyword; it attributes genuineness/properness.

trigger_variants.translation_warning: Map exact form before translating.
May encode stronger polemic than 'authentic'.
Check whether source wording was authenticity, truth, or purity.
Code only when the phrase authorizes flamenco value, not generic sincerity.
Code only when the phrase authorizes flamenco value, not generic correctness.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: contribuyendo a que los menos iniciados sintonicen con el auténtico Flamenco que desde las Peñas siempre hemos pregonado
few_shot_examples.rationale: The passage explicitly presents a form of flamenco as auténtico and links that authenticity to peña-based authority.

few_shot_examples.rationale: This is a compact English lexical marker for authenticity discourse.

few_shot_examples.rationale: This uses the trigger word auténtica but violates the negative constraint because it modifies the emotional meaning of a homage, not the authenticity of flamenco.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: This is authentic Chinese-American food.
few_shot_examples.rationale: This uses the trigger word authentic but violates the negative constraint because it is an analogy about restaurant food, not an authenticity claim about flamenco.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: ¿verdad Tío Joaquín?
few_shot_examples.rationale: This uses the trigger word verdad but violates the negative constraint because it is conversational confirmation, not an authenticity marker.

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Bendix shows authenticity functioning as a means to define a field, distinguish valued culture from other forms, and authorize methods or paradigms.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Use this as the basis for coding authenticity by discursive function, not as an inherent property.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Regina Bendix, In Search of Authenticity (1997), p. 5 & p. 7
theoretical_anchors.summary: "Authenticity, I argue, was variously used as an agent to define this subject, differentiate it from other cultural manifestations, develop methods of analysis, critique competing theories, or create new paradigms." (p. 5) Furthermore, "Declaring something authentic legitimated the subject that was declared authentic, and the declaration in turn can legitimate the authenticator" (p. 7).

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Bendix lists a recurring authenticity vocabulary: original, genuine, natural, noble, innocent, lively, sensuous, stirring.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Use exact lexical markers as evidence, but do not stop there; connect them to larger discourse function.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Regina Bendix, In Search of Authenticity (1997), p. 15
theoretical_anchors.summary: "Original, genuine, natural, naive, noble and innocent, lively, sensuous, stirring—the string of adjectives could be continued. Folklorists since the eighteenth century have used them to circumscribe the longed-for quality that they saw encapsulated at first in folklore texts and later in folklore performance." (p. 15)

AUTH_02.definition: Language that defines proper flamenco by excluding or devaluing what is impure, fake, spurious, diluted, artificial, corrupted, or not real flamenco.
AUTH_02.use_when: Use when purity/contamination, genuine/fake, or proper/improper rhetoric draws a boundary around legitimate flamenco.
AUTH_02.do_not_use_when: Do not use for stylistic difference, factual correction, or preference without evaluative exclusion.
required_conditions: A boundary is drawn between legitimate/proper and illegitimate/improper forms.
An excluded or devalued target can be identified.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: flamenco puro-genuine flamenco. This is not the Hollywood or Las Vegas version.

few_shot_examples.rationale: This uses the trigger idea falsa but violates the negative constraint because it concerns factual correction, not a genuine/spurious flamenco binary.

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Bendix frames authenticity against inauthenticity/spuriousness and shows market or ideological forces treated as spoiling agents.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Supports codes for purity boundary work and anti-commercial contamination.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Regina Bendix, In Search of Authenticity (1997), p. 9
theoretical_anchors.summary: "[E]fforts to promote and market folklore invariably lead to a perceived loss of authenticity, because students of culture until recent years have considered ideological and market forces as outside agents that spoil folklore's authenticity... identifying some cultural expressions or artifacts as authentic, genuine, trustworthy, or legitimate simultaneously implies that other manifestations are fake, spurious, and even illegitimate." (p. 9)

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Identifying something as authentic simultaneously creates its opposite: the fake or spurious.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Supports coding the genuine/spurious dichotomy when texts define flamenco against fake or adulterated forms.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Richard Handler and Jocelyn Linnekin, 'Tradition, Genuine or Spurious' (1984) & Regina Bendix (1997) p. 9
theoretical_anchors.summary: Handler & Linnekin interrogate Sapir's 'genuine and spurious' binary. Bendix notes that identifying something as authentic "simultaneously implies that other manifestations are fake, spurious, and even illegitimate." (p. 9)

AUTH_03.definition: Language that grounds flamenco value in tradition, continuity, roots, origin, survival, inheritance, or faithful continuation of a valued past.
AUTH_03.use_when: Use when tradition, continuity, preservation, roots, origin, or inheritance carries evaluative authority for present flamenco.
AUTH_03.do_not_use_when: Do not use for neutral chronology, bare age, etymology, or origin stories without present-value or authority stakes.
required_conditions: The past is used to authorize, value, preserve, or judge a present practice.
The text implies continuity, rootedness, or origin as meaningful for flamenco.

trigger_variants.translation_warning: Do not assume stable inherited core.
Do not assume stable inherited core.
May conceal selective reconstruction.
May conceal selective reconstruction.
Roots claims are not just chronology.
Roots claims are not just chronology.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: Y hoy los tenemos vigentes y rehabilitados en toda su pureza gracias a la «tradición oral»
few_shot_examples.rationale: Tradition is invoked as the mechanism that authorizes present continuity and purity.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: I do the cante my own way, naturally without departing from the traditional boundaries.
few_shot_examples.rationale: Tradition is invoked as an authoritative boundary for proper performance.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: vamos a conservar los fandangos personales como patrimonio de sus creadores que sólo a título de evocación singular y en actos definidos, deben ser cantados
few_shot_examples.rationale: The passage calls for conserving repertoire as a continuing inheritance tied to its creators.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: Upon returning to Santa Fe in 1964, he began a tradition which has continued uninterrupted for 27 years.
few_shot_examples.rationale: The passage constructs continuity across time through an uninterrupted local tradition.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: UNA TRADICION QUE MANTENEMOS DIA TRAS DIA CERVEZAS El Alcázar
few_shot_examples.rationale: This uses the trigger word tradición but violates the negative constraint because it is advertising copy, not a flamenco tradition claim.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: traditional flamenco roots with contemporary dance music
few_shot_examples.rationale: This uses the trigger word traditional but violates the negative constraint because it is promotional genre description rather than a tradition claim authorizing properness.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: Todavía conservo en la carpeta de mi mesa su última tarjeta de Navidad.
few_shot_examples.rationale: This uses the trigger word conservo but violates the negative constraint because it refers to a personal object, not cultural continuity.

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Handler and Linnekin argue that tradition cannot be defined by boundedness, givenness, or essence, but is an interpretive process.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Supports coding tradition as a claim or construction rather than an objective inheritance.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Richard Handler and Jocelyn Linnekin, 'Tradition, Genuine or Spurious' (1984), p. 273
theoretical_anchors.summary: "We have concluded that tradition cannot be defined in terms of boundedness, givenness, or essence. Rather, tradition refers to an interpretive process that embodies both continuity and discontinuity." (p. 273)

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Continuity with the past is constructed in the present; tradition is symbolic process, not approximate identity of an objective thing.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Use for continuity, preservation, survival, and faithful-transmission rhetoric.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Richard Handler and Jocelyn Linnekin, 'Tradition, Genuine or Spurious' (1984), p. 287
theoretical_anchors.summary: "Thus we can no longer speak of tradition in terms of the approximate identity of some objective thing that changes while remaining the same. Instead, we must understand tradition as a symbolic process that both presupposes past symbolisms and creatively reinterprets them." (p. 287)

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Authenticity relies on the search for origins and the 'soul of the people' as the essence of cultural value.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Use when texts ground cultural authority and legitimacy in roots, origins, and primary essence.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Regina Bendix (1997) p. 6 & p. 19
theoretical_anchors.summary: Authenticity acts as the "origin and essence of being human" (p. 6) and relies on the "exuberant search for the 'soul of the people'" (p. 19). Roots/origin claims are the rhetorical mechanisms for securing this essence.

AUTH_04.definition: Language that treats commercial spectacle, tourism, mass mediation, or staged/public distance as weakening authenticity, or treats intimate/social co-presence as more authentic.
AUTH_04.use_when: Use when markets, tourism, publicity, spectacle, or formal stage separation are framed as threats to real flamenco, or intimacy/co-presence is framed as evidence of real flamenco.
AUTH_04.do_not_use_when: Do not use for routine sales, sponsorship, publication economics, generic emotional intimacy, or event setting descriptions without authenticity stakes.
required_conditions: Commercial/public/spectacular or intimate/private/social setting is linked to authenticity or loss of authenticity.

trigger_variants.translation_warning: Needs authenticity stakes, not just economics.
Needs authenticity stakes, not just economics.
Do not confuse with generic sentimentality.
Needs evaluative authenticity force.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: se ha sacado de su círculo original comercializándose y desposeyéndole de parte de sus valores reales
few_shot_examples.rationale: Commercialization is treated as removing flamenco from its original circle and stripping real values.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: the art will have to withdraw once more with the "purists" if it is to protect its vitality and to avoid the twin threats of academicism and commercialization
few_shot_examples.rationale: Commercialization is named as a threat to flamenco vitality and authenticity.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: pierde su enorme valor de intimidad, de hablar al oído del hermano, pero en cambio en los café-cantantes se va a engrandecer horizontalmente
few_shot_examples.rationale: Intimacy and closeness are treated as evidence of a more authentic earlier flamenco.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: flamenco is at its purest when shared between musicians and a few onlookers in marathon, all-night sessions. These "juergas" usually occur in intimate settings
few_shot_examples.rationale: Intimacy, small scale, and co-presence are treated as evidence of flamenco at its purest.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: patrocinado por la Diputación de Granada, el Ayuntamiento de Cúllar de Vega y firmas comerciales
few_shot_examples.rationale: This uses the trigger word comerciales but violates the negative constraint because it is routine sponsorship information without authenticity stakes.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: I am presently looking into a source for commercial videos of flamenco performances from Spain
few_shot_examples.rationale: This uses the trigger word commercial but violates the negative constraint because it is routine video distribution information without authenticity judgment.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: en un ritual que conlleva una mágica intimidad con él
few_shot_examples.rationale: This uses the trigger word intimidad but violates the negative constraint because it describes symbolic intimacy in villancico imagery, not flamenco authenticity.

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Commercialization and tourist-oriented spectacles are treated as outside agents that spoil authenticity.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Supports coding anti-commercial sentiment when market forces are framed as corrupting genuine flamenco.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Regina Bendix (1997) p. 9 & Timothy deWaal Malefyt (1998) p. 63
theoretical_anchors.summary: Bendix observes that "efforts to promote and market folklore invariably lead to a perceived loss of authenticity... market forces [are] outside agents that spoil folklore's authenticity" (p. 9). Malefyt contrasts authentic peña practice against "commercial venues for purposes of tourism" (p. 63).

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Malefyt's peña scenes treat intimacy, familiarity, crowding, shared attention, and emotional density as signs of a more real and valued flamenco than the tourist-oriented tablao.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Supports coding intimacy as a marker of authenticity rather than mere atmosphere.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Timothy deWaal Malefyt, '"Inside" and "Outside" Spanish Flamenco' (1998), p. 63
theoretical_anchors.summary: "At the center of the flamenco tradition are Andalusian flamenco aficionados who practice an intimate, private, and emotional exchange of flamenco in exclusive peña clubs, which directly contrast flamenco performed publicly and spectacularly in commercial venues for purposes of tourism." (p. 63)

HERIT.purpose: Track patrimonialization, public heritage value, safeguarding, official recognition, institutional heritage authority, living heritage, memory, and contested community heritage.
HERIT.use_when: Use when passages invoke patrimonio/heritage, safeguarding, listing, institutional recognition, public cultural value, memory, or heritage management.
HERIT.do_not_use_when: Do not use for authenticity, roots, lineage, or tradition unless the passage also shifts into public-culture, institutional, or patrimonial framing.

HERIT_01.definition: Language that frames flamenco as heritage or patrimony and treats value through public culture, collective identity, memory, recognition, or transmission.
HERIT_01.use_when: Use when patrimonio/heritage is a category of public value, identity, memory, or cultural policy.
HERIT_01.do_not_use_when: Do not use when heritage means personal ancestry, literary stock, or vague legacy without public cultural heritage framing.
required_conditions: The heritage/patrimony frame concerns flamenco or a related cultural practice.
The passage treats heritage as public/collective cultural value.
do_not_code_if: Patrimonio as one person's literary assets.

trigger_variants.translation_warning: May mark institutional value rather than authenticity.
Check whether original wording was patrimonio, tradition, or legacy.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: Todos tenemos el deber y derecho irrenunciable de conservar el patrimonio cultural que se nos ha entregado.
few_shot_examples.rationale: Flamenco is framed as patrimonio cultural and as a collective public responsibility.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: The purpose of these presentations was to enhance the students' and general public's awareness regarding the art of flamenco and its influences on the cultural heritage of the area.
few_shot_examples.rationale: Flamenco is framed as cultural heritage and public cultural value.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: constituía el patrimonio literario de Balmaseda
few_shot_examples.rationale: This uses the trigger word patrimonio but violates the negative constraint because it refers to one writer's literary stock, not public heritage discourse.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: Támara is a small woman... with a pretty face that clearly shows the Mediterranean in her heritage.
few_shot_examples.rationale: This uses the trigger word heritage but violates the negative constraint because it refers to ancestry/appearance, not public cultural heritage discourse.

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Smith argues that heritage is not a thing but a cultural and social process that constructs and negotiates identities, values, and meanings in the present.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Use to keep heritage discourse analytically separate from authenticity or tradition claims.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Laurajane Smith, Uses of Heritage (2006), p. 11 & p. 44
theoretical_anchors.summary: "There is, really, no such thing as heritage... ‘Heritage’ is therefore ultimately a cultural practice, involved in the construction and regulation of a range of values and understandings." (p. 11) It is a cultural process that identifies what can be given meaning and value as heritage (p. 44).

HERIT_02.definition: Heritage discourse that privileges experts, institutions, official recognition, listing, inscription, proclamation, conservation, consensus, or state/public authority.
HERIT_02.use_when: Use when an institution, expert, listing, inventory, official recognition, or authorized heritage mechanism defines or valorizes flamenco.
HERIT_02.do_not_use_when: Do not use for grassroots memory, community pride, or ordinary recognition unless official/institutional heritage authorization is explicit.

The passage is about heritage authority, not ordinary event sponsorship.

Generic praise by an organization without patrimonial framing.

trigger_variants.translation_warning: Do not impose as actor language.

Check if value comes from official recognition.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: yo hice unas declaraciones

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Smith defines an authorized heritage discourse that privileges expert authority, monumentality, innate significance, social consensus, and nation-building.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Supports coding institutional authority and official public-culture framing.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Laurajane Smith, Uses of Heritage (2006), p. 11 & p. 29
theoretical_anchors.summary: "The ‘authorized heritage discourse’ privileges monumentality and grand scale, innate artefact/site significance tied to time depth, scientific/aesthetic expert judgement, social consensus and nation building." (p. 11) It defines who the legitimate spokespersons for the past are, specifically experts (p. 29).

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Kirshenblatt-Gimblett shows that listing and inscription are metacultural artifacts: the list is the context for everything on it and confers value symbolically.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Supports listing, inventory, inscription, and valorization codes.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Barbara Kirshenblatt-Gimblett, 'Intangible Heritage as Metacultural Production' (2004), p. 55
theoretical_anchors.summary: "Some of those involved in the process of developing the intangible heritage initiative had hoped for cultural rather than metacultural outcomes; they wanted to focus on actions that would directly support local cultural reproduction, rather than on creating metacultural artefacts such as the list." (p. 55)

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: UNESCO (and similar cultural institutions) shifted from preserving records of disappearing traditions to sustaining living traditions by supporting practitioners and conditions for cultural reproduction.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Use for safeguarding and policy language focused on support infrastructures rather than authenticity.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Barbara Kirshenblatt-Gimblett, 'Intangible Heritage as Metacultural Production' (2004), p. 53
theoretical_anchors.summary: "The most recent model seeks to sustain a living, if endangered, tradition by supporting the conditions necessary for cultural reproduction. This means according value to the ‘carriers’ and ‘transmitters’ of traditions, as well as to their habitus and habitat." (p. 53)

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Intangible heritage is alive; the task is to sustain the whole system as a living entity, not merely collect intangible artifacts.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Use when passages emphasize living practice, people, habitat, or conditions for reproduction.

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Smith presents heritage as contested, political, and usable by subaltern groups to negotiate control, identity, and social meaning.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Use when heritage is the terrain of dispute rather than a consensus good.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Laurajane Smith, Uses of Heritage (2006), p. 7
theoretical_anchors.summary: "Part III... examines subaltern uses of heritage, and explores the various ways authorized and received notions of heritage and the values they represent are contested... theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Smith treats heritage as something communities use to remember, belong, negotiate change, and contest control, not only as expert designation.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Supports a distinction between vernacular/community heritage use and authorized heritage discourse.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Laurajane Smith, Uses of Heritage (2006), p. 7 & p. 1
theoretical_anchors.summary: "Commemoration and remembrance are used as platforms from which the community is continually redefining and remaking both itself and the social networks that bind the people of the community together." (p. 7) Communities do 'heritage work' by "being in place, renewing memories and associations, sharing experiences with kinswomen to cement present and future social and familial relationships." (p. 1)

theoretical_anchors.excerpt: Heritage is a process of engagement, an act of communication and meaning-making in the present, tied to memory, performance, place, and identity.
theoretical_anchors.rationale: Supports coding heritage as lived experience and identity-work, not only as policy or recognition.
theoretical_anchors.literature_source: Laurajane Smith, Uses of Heritage (2006), p. 1
theoretical_anchors.summary: "Heritage wasn’t only about the past – though it was that too – it also wasn’t just about material things – though it was that as well – heritage was a process of engagement, an act of communication and an act of making meaning in and for the present." (p. 1)

CRIT_01.use_when: Use when the passage evaluates quality, success, failure, seriousness, originality, artistry, or value.
CRIT_01.do_not_use_when: Do not use for neutral description, listing, or biography without evaluative judgment.
required_conditions: The passage makes an evaluative judgment.
The evaluated target is identifiable.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: Antonio Núñez «El Chocolate» gustó, hizo sentir la verdad desnuda de Andalucía, en una palabra: comunicó.
few_shot_examples.rationale: The passage explicitly judges a performance's success and expressive force.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: There was a lack of what the Spaniards call DUENDE, a lack of that personal sense of matador-tragedy that is the essence of Spanish dance at its noblest and most ennobling.
few_shot_examples.rationale: A critic evaluates the performance by naming the absence of duende as a quality failure.

few_shot_examples.rationale: Pobre means unfortunate here; it is not a quality judgment about the singer's flamenco artistry.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: This comparison is not referring to praise or criticism, but rather to pure observation.

CRIT_02.definition: Language that defines flamenco quality through criteria such as compás, duende, depth, restraint, power, technique, expression, purity, or emotional force.
CRIT_02.use_when: Use when the passage names or applies aesthetic criteria to define what counts as good flamenco.
CRIT_02.do_not_use_when: Do not use for mere mention of technical terms without judging or defining quality.
required_conditions: An aesthetic criterion is named or applied.
The criterion helps judge, define, or explain flamenco value.
do_not_code_if: Technical vocabulary in a purely descriptive/instructional context.

trigger_variants.translation_warning: Requires evaluative function.
Requires evaluative function.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: Su quejío fue duende despierto... Su compás nos arrebató por bulerías. Por siguiriyas nos hirió en lo más profundo del ser.
few_shot_examples.rationale: Duende, compás, and depth are applied as criteria for judging flamenco quality.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: There was a lack of what the Spaniards call DUENDE, a lack of that personal sense of matador-tragedy that is the essence of Spanish dance at its noblest and most ennobling.
few_shot_examples.rationale: Duende is used as a criterion for judging depth and nobility in performance.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: Este estado que llaman duende no es otra cosa que el resultado del proceso llamado por Aristóteles catarsis o purga de las emociones.
few_shot_examples.rationale: Duende is discussed as a historical/theoretical concept, not applied as an evaluative criterion for a flamenco performance.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: A change in the strum pattern alerts the dancers that the introductory melody will start at the beginning of the next compas.
few_shot_examples.rationale: Compas is used as a technical timing term, not as an evaluative criterion.

theoretical_anchors.summary: Wieczorek summarizes disputes over pure/commercial and traditional/contemporary flamenco; Washabaugh cautions that such criteria are historically contested.

CRIT_03.do_not_use_when: Do not use for simple comparison without value hierarchy.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: the best cantaor of this century... 50 glorious years of authentic mastership in this difficult world of flamenco.
few_shot_examples.rationale: The passage canonizes Antonio Mairena through superlative ranking and enduring master status.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: Se suele llamar «cante jondo» a ciertos cantes estimados superiores. El Flamenco abarca todas las modalidades conocidas de «cante» sin establecer jerarquías ni involucrar valoraciones.

few_shot_examples.excerpt: La mejor organización al servicio del espectáculo mundial Siempre a sus órdenes

CRIT_04.definition: Language that grants critics, scholars, reviewers, editors, flamencologists, or expert voices authority, or uses critique to police commercial, staged, tourist, pure, hybrid, or improper flamenco.
CRIT_04.use_when: Use when expert critical voice or review discourse authorizes judgment, or when criticism enforces boundaries around proper/improper flamenco.
CRIT_04.do_not_use_when: Do not use for ordinary opinion without expert/critical authority or boundary stakes.
required_conditions: A critic/expert/reviewer/editor or critical discourse is positioned as authoritative, or critique polices flamenco boundaries.
The target and evaluative basis are identifiable.

annotation_rules.evidence_rule: Every positive code must include a direct quote from the visible review text and a one-sentence rationale.
annotation_rules.keyword_rule: Lexical triggers are retrieval aids, not sufficient evidence. Code only when the required discourse function is present.
annotation_rules.truncation_rule: For truncated articles, annotate only the visible excerpt and mark insufficient_context=true when missing context prevents a reliable decision.
annotation_rules.multi_label_rule: Multiple primary codes may be assigned to the same evidence span only when each code's required conditions are independently satisfied.
